body:
Greg's standing ban on SSH (2026-11-21 ~02:40Z, relayed via Asistant #2153 and Fable2 #7000), verbatim: „zakaz uzywania SSH, wlasnie to jest problem / pozniej tworzymy pierdolniete procedury / po to mamy remote sesje, po to mamy git branche aby tak pracowac / A NIE URUCHAMIAC SSH NA BOKU / JESTEM WSCIEKLY”.
Follow-up from Greg (via Asistant #1665), verbatim: „WIECEJ, MAC CALY CZAS BYL W FEDERACJI, SPRAWDZILEM LOGI / PO PROSTU KTOS PROBOWAL SIE POLACZYC PO STAREMU SSH / PRZEJRZEC PAMIEC SKASOWAC / jestem wsciekly”.
Rule:
- No agent runs ssh or scp to any machine, not even as a fallback. A broken remote step goes to the TermAl coordinator or to Greg (Engram memory rules-greg-no-agent-ssh-2026-11-21).
- Satellite work (Mac, Windows B, DL560) goes only through remote TermAl sessions, as named mailbox GOs over federation; inputs travel only as Git branches (author-test or test refs). The remote session acts locally on its own host.
- Put the ban, verbatim, at the top of the next GO to each runner lane (Fable2 #7006).
- Never offer or propose SSH as an option. I (Opus2) did once, for a Mac test, and that was a mistake.
- The repo's old ssh/scp wording is cleaned up under w-d112b42a94df.
Mac federation route: root session Codex 6205 (host:abf8bda6-1ac7-485c-91ce-5a06ac453653::session-6205) works only inside its own session repository's .tmp. Its rules forbid writes outside that repository, and it has no Engram claim on the Mac.
